recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-17905 unless the work group later decides to further clarify the semantics of printed page counts.
issue_request: FHIR-17905 requested a core extension on DocumentReference.content.attachment or Attachment to indicate the number of pages in an attached document. The issue is Published/Persuasive and its resolution says the request was already applied to Attachment.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly tagged FHIR-17905 was found. Attachment.pages was added by commit 5c62f91cd81f150be72ad506c876e3cc20bd631d, the Media-to-DocumentReference merge tagged GF#19250; the FHIR-19250 Jira comments state that branch included page count on Attachment for GF#17905.
additional_context: The original Zulip thread records the scanned-document metadata use case and discussion of Attachment/core-extension scope. MnM minutes from 2021-02-17 record a 4-0-1 Persuasive vote. The current source keeps the concept at Attachment scope, which also covers DocumentReference.content.attachment.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scope source already provides a 0..1 positiveInt Attachment.pages element with definition 'The number of pages when printed'; adding a redundant extension or DocumentReference-specific prose would not improve conformance behavior.

related_jiras.note: The source commit tagged GF#19250 added Attachment.pages and its Jira comments explicitly say that page count was included for GF#17905.
This later Attachment-size issue is in the same Media-to-DocumentReference consolidation family, but it is separate from deciding whether FHIR-17905 is already satisfied.
